newsitem.title: UK: Euro oil swaps mixed, LS fuel dips $2 but CFDs gain.
newsitem.headline: Euro oil swaps mixed, LS fuel dips $2 but CFDs gain.

text.p: European oil swaps ended mixed but quiet on Monday with modest gains on Brent crude CFDs but a drop of $2 a tonne on low sulphur fuel.
Brent CFDs for the next few weeks were roughly flat at 32 cents under June after gaining up to five cents.
The move flattened out the modest contango seen last week althougth the contango remained in place for further forward periods.

Values against front line IPE Brent were 32 cents under for May with June 24 cents under and July 20 cents under. The third and fourth quarters were 15 cents and 13 cents under respectively with the whole of 1998 talking either side of six cents under the screen.
Heavy fuel swaps slipped $2 a tonne for low sulphur fuel with May dipping at one point to $84.75 before steadying towards the close. June talked $1 a tonne higher and July another $1 higher.
May barges were less weak with May down just $1 to $82 and a less steep contango into June and July of about 50 cents a month.
"The high-lows came into about $3.50. But the fall in low sulphur was just due to a couple of physical cargoes which are unsold," said a trader.
Meanwhile, middle distllates were little changed. Gas oil was flat despite confirmation of a German tender to buy 500,000 tonnes of middle distillate this summer.
Crack spreads against Brent talked $4.30 a barrel (3Q97), $4.85 (4Q97), $4.70 (1Q98), $4.10 (2Q98).
Jet premiums above the IPE also held steady. May was pegged around $24.50 a tonne over while June was $25.00 over.
Gasoline held at $195 for May but trade was thin. June was pegged around $193 with crack spreads also flat at $5.25 a barrel and $4.90 for the the two months respectively.
